summary: First checkpoint of the blueprint for Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology and Iwasawa cohomology, within RS-08's boundaries. L0: the p-adic completion of a multiplicative group and its comparison with the tensor product (true for global units and S-units, false for local multiplicative groups and for F^×), the Kummer maps along the μ_{p^m} tower, the Mittag-Leffler bookkeeping, the identification H^1(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ lim K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} and its S-unit form H^1(G_{F,S}, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ ℤ_p ⊗ 𝓞_{F,S}^×. L2: the generic Selmer-kernel API (local conditions, strict and relaxed modifications, change of conditions, functoriality, propagation, the passage V → T, W with saturation), the unramified and Greenberg conditions, Galois Selmer groups, Pontryagin duals and coranks, and the elliptic p^∞-Selmer group. Two new findings in RJW are recorded. Second checkpoint: L1's parametric pairing lemmas (orthogonal complements, compatibility of the local pairings for T, V, W, W_M), and in L2 the dual Selmer structure, the unramified dimension count and bad-prime comparison terms, local duality for the finite conditions on V, T and W_M, Selmer groups as limits, and Poitou–Tate for Selmer groups (Rubin Theorem 7.3, Corollary 7.5), built on ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4's Poitou–Tate. Third checkpoint: L3 from Nekovář, Selmer complexes, 8.3–8.4 and Rubin Appendix B §§3–5: Iwasawa cohomology by corestriction, Shapiro's lemma over Λ with the inverse action, descent and control spectral sequences, the torsion criterion, universal norms, semilocal cohomology and the cyclotomic twist. Checkpoint 4 (cc-39fac3) starts L4 from RJW §§10.5, 13.5: Iwasawa cohomology of local units and the cyclotomic Euler system, Greenberg Selmer groups of Tate twists and X_∞^+, criticality of ℚ_p(n), the Iwasawa–Greenberg conjecture as a proposition with its even-twist case proved from Theorem 13.8, and the Bloch–Kato condition; findings E4–E5.

nodes.title: Completion of global units
nodes.statement: For a number field F, the unit group E_F = 𝓞_F^× is finitely generated, so ℤ_p ⊗ E_F ≅ Ê_F; and the map Ê_F → (F^×)^ induced by E_F ⊆ F^× is injective, because E_F ∩ (F^×)^{p^m} = E_F^{p^m}: a p^m-th root in F of a unit is a unit.
hypotheses: F a number field, p prime, m ≥ 0.
proofSteps: E_F is finitely generated by Dirichlet's theorem (NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod: every unit is torsion times a product of fundamental units); apply padic-completion.
If x ∈ F^× and x^{p^m} = u ∈ E_F, then x and x^{−1} are integral over 𝓞_F (IsIntegral.of_pow), so x ∈ E_F.
Hence the subspace topology on E_F from the p-adic topology of F^× is its own p-adic topology, and the completion map is injective.
acceptance: The image is closed but not all of (F^×)^; the quotient (F^×)^/Ê_F involves the ideal group.

An element of F^× whose p^m-th power is an S-unit has valuation zero outside S, so it is an S-unit; conclude as in units-completion.

nodes.title: Completion of a local multiplicative group
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ, with K^× = π^ℤ × 𝓞_K^× and 𝓞_K^× = μ_{q−1} × U^1_K. Then (K^×)^ ≅ ℤ_p × (𝓞_K^×)^, where (𝓞_K^×)^ = U^1_K if ℓ = p (a finitely generated ℤ_p-module) and (𝓞_K^×)^ = μ_{p^∞}(K) if ℓ ≠ p (U^1_K is pro-ℓ, hence p-divisible). The map K^× ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p → (K^×)^ is surjective but not injective, so for local fields the completion does not agree with the algebraic tensor product.
hypotheses: K/ℚ_ℓ finite, ℓ any prime (ℓ = p allowed).
proofSteps: The decomposition K^× = π^ℤ × μ_{q−1} × U^1_K and the structure of U^1_K come from Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification Layer 1 (requested).
Completion commutes with finite products; ℤ̂ = ℤ_p; μ_{q−1} contributes its p-part; U^1_K is already p-adically complete (ℓ = p) or p-divisible (ℓ ≠ p).
Non-injectivity for ℓ = p: U^1_K ⊇ ℤ_p, and ℤ_p ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p → ℤ_p kills a ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ a, which is nonzero for a ∉ ℚ because ℤ_p ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p ⊆ ℚ_p ⊗_ℚ ℚ_p.
acceptance: For ℓ ≠ p, the kernel contains U^1_K ⊗ ℤ_p ≠ 0.

H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}) ≅ K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} by Kummer theory (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9).

A system of finite sets is Mittag-Leffler (CategoryTheory.Functor.isMittagLeffler_of_exists_finite_range).

nodes.title: The p-adic Kummer identification
nodes.statement: For a field K with p invertible, H^1(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ lim_m K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} = (K^×)^, where ℤ_p(1) = lim μ_{p^m} is a compact coefficient module and H^1 is continuous-cochain cohomology (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1). The map is H^1(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) → lim_m H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}), an isomorphism because the Milnor term lim^1 H^0(G_K, μ_{p^m}) vanishes, followed by κ_∞^{−1}. It is an algebraic isomorphism for every K; when every K^×/(K^×)^{p^m} is finite (local fields) both sides are profinite and it is a homeomorphism. It is compatible with restriction and with corestriction versus the norm for finite separable extensions.
hypotheses: p invertible in K. No finite generation of K^× is assumed; the target is the completion, not K^× ⊗ ℤ_p.
proofSteps: Milnor sequence 0 → lim^1 H^0(G_K, μ_{p^m}) → H^1(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) → lim H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}) → 0 (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.1; Rubin Proposition B.2.3).
roots-of-unity-mittag-leffler kills the lim^1 term.
kummer-limit-map identifies the limit with (K^×)^.
For local K, local-power-class-finite makes both sides profinite, and a continuous bijection of compact Hausdorff groups is a homeomorphism.
acceptance: For K = ℚ the identification holds with the completion, and ℚ^× ⊗ ℤ_p → H^1(G_ℚ, ℤ_p(1)) is not surjective (sourceIssues E1).

nodes.title: The Kummer identification for S-units
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field and S a finite set of places containing those above p and ∞. Then H^1(G_{F,S}, ℤ_p(1)) ≅ ℤ_p ⊗ 𝓞_{F,S}^×, compatibly with restriction to finite extensions inside F_S and with corestriction versus the norm.
hypotheses: S ⊇ {v | p∞}, so μ_{p^m} is a G_{F,S}-module and p is an S-unit.
proofSteps: The Kummer sequence for G_{F,S}: 0 → 𝓞_{F,S}^×/p^m → H^1(G_{F,S}, μ_{p^m}) → Pic(𝓞_{F,S})[p^m] → 0 (ArithmeticGaloisDuality:R02.3).
Pass to the limit: roots-of-unity-mittag-leffler removes lim^1 H^0; the terms 𝓞_{F,S}^×/p^m are finite; lim_m Pic[p^m] = T_p Pic = 0 because Pic(𝓞_{F,S}) is finite.
lim 𝓞_{F,S}^×/p^m = ℤ_p ⊗ 𝓞_{F,S}^× (s-units-completion).
acceptance: This is the finite-level statement behind Burungale–Tian's units-kummer item; the tower limit belongs to L3.

nodes.title: Which inverse-limit hypotheses hold
nodes.statement: For the towers used in this roadmap: (a) for every field K, lim^1_m μ_{p^m}(K) = 0; (b) for K local, every H^1(G_K, μ_{p^m}) is finite, so the H^1 system is Mittag-Leffler and H^2(G_K, ℤ_p(1)) = lim_m H^2(G_K, μ_{p^m}); (c) for G_{F,S} with S ⊇ {v | p∞}, every H^1(G_{F,S}, μ_{p^m}) is finite, with the same consequence; (d) for the full G_F of a number field, H^1(G_F, μ_{p^m}) = F^×/(F^×)^{p^m} is infinite, and no Mittag-Leffler argument is available for H^2(G_F, ℤ_p(1)).

(b) local-power-class-finite and Rubin Proposition B.2.3 with i = 2.
(c) The Kummer sequence of s-unit-kummer-identification has finite outer terms.
(d) F^× contains a free abelian group on the primes.

nodes.title: Selmer data
nodes.statement: Selmer data over a commutative ring R indexed by a set of places ι: a global R-module H (for example H^1(G_{K,Σ}, M)), local R-modules H_v (for example H^1(K_v, M)), R-linear localisation maps res_v : H → H_v, and local conditions L_v ⊆ H_v (R-submodules). Modifications replace the conditions: relaxed (L_v = H_v) on a set of places, strict (L_v = 0) on a set of places.

nodes.title: Orthogonal complements of local conditions
nodes.statement: Let O be the ring of integers of a finite extension Φ of ℚ_p, D = Φ/O, and b : X × X′ → Y a bilinear pairing of O-modules (Y = Φ, O/MO or D). For an O-submodule F ⊆ X, F^⊥ = {x′ ∈ X′ : b(F, x′) = 0}. Applied to the local Tate pairings H¹(K, A) × H¹(K, A^*) → Y for A = V, W_M, T and A^* = V^*, W^*_M, W^* (Rubin, Theorem 4.1), F^⊥ is the dual local condition F^* of Mazur–Rubin, Definition 1.6.
hypotheses: b bilinear; perfectness, where used, is a hypothesis of the lemma that uses it.
proofSteps: F^⊥ is an O-submodule, and F ↦ F^⊥ is antitone.

If b is perfect (nondegenerate on both sides) and X is finite, a finite-dimensional Φ-space, or a finitely generated O-module paired perfectly with a cofinitely generated one, then F^⊥⊥ = F: in the last case every finitely generated submodule is closed, and Pontryagin duality applies.
Image and preimage: if π : X → Z and ι : Z′ → X′ are adjoint (b_Z(π x, z′) = b(x, ι z′)), then (π F)^⊥ = ι^{−1}(F^⊥); dually (π^{−1} G)^⊥ = ι(G^⊥) when b and b_Z are perfect.
Counting: for X finite and b perfect, #F · #F^⊥ = #X; for Φ-spaces, dim F + dim F^⊥ = dim X.
If F^⊥ = F′, then b induces a perfect pairing (X/F) × F′ → Y.
acceptance: The parametric lemma RS-08 asks L1 to state before L2 instantiates named conditions.
Stated for a named pairing; a statement quantified over arbitrary pairings would admit the zero pairing, for which F^⊥ = X′ for every F.

nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ, ℝ or ℂ and T a p-adic representation of G_K. For the lattice and rational pairings, the continuous cochains and limits are those of ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1.

The dual Selmer structure F^* on T^* = Hom(T, μ_{p^∞}) has Σ(F^*) = Σ(F) and H¹_{F^*}(K_q, T^*) = H¹_F(K_q, T)^⊥ under the local Tate pairing (Mazur–Rubin, Definition 2.5).

The dual conditions are orthogonal-complement for the local Tate pairings.

nodes.title: Dimensions of unramified classes
nodes.statement: Let K/ℚ_ℓ be finite with ℓ ≠ p and V a finite-dimensional ℚ_p[G_K]-module. Then dim H¹_ur(K, V) = dim V^{G_K}, and dim H¹(K, V)/H¹_ur(K, V) = dim H²(K, V).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p.
proofSteps: unramified-condition: H¹_ur(K, V) = V^I/(Fr − 1)V^I, so 0 → V^{G_K} → V^I → V^I → H¹_ur(K, V) → 0 gives (i).

I has a unique maximal subgroup I′ of pro-order prime to p with I/I′ ≅ ℤ_p (the tame quotient, LocalFieldsRamification Layer 4), so I and Gal(K^ur/K) have p-cohomological dimension 1 (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 11).

Hochschild–Serre (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2) gives H¹(K^ur/K, H¹(I, V)) = H²(K, V) and H¹(K, V)/H¹_ur(K, V) = H¹(I, V)^{Fr=1}; the sequence 0 → H¹/H¹_ur → H¹(I, V) → H¹(I, V) → H²(K, V) → 0 gives (ii).
acceptance: Only for ℓ ≠ p; at ℓ = p the finite condition is chosen, not computed.

nodes.title: Finite against unramified classes at bad primes
nodes.statement: Let K/ℚ_ℓ be finite with ℓ ≠ p, H¹_f(K, V) = H¹_ur(K, V), and H¹_f(K, T), H¹_f(K, W), H¹_f(K, W_M) as in lattice-passage. Put 𝒲 = W^I/(W^I)_div, a finite module. (i) H¹_f(K, W) = H¹_ur(K, W)_div. (ii) H¹_ur(K, T) ⊆ H¹_f(K, T) with finite index, and H¹_s(K, T) is torsion-free. (iii) H¹_ur(K, W)/H¹_f(K, W) ≅ 𝒲/(Fr − 1)𝒲 and H¹_f(K, T)/H¹_ur(K, T) ≅ 𝒲^{Fr=1}. (iv) If T is unramified, H¹_f = H¹_ur for T and W. Moreover H¹_f(K, W_M) is the image of H¹_f(K, T), and equals H¹_ur(K, W_M) when T is unramified. At an archimedean place H¹_f(K, W) = 0, H¹_f(K, T) = H¹(K, T) and H¹_f(K, W_M) = W^{G_K}/M W^{G_K}, all zero unless K = ℝ and p = 2.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p for (i)–(iv); T a lattice.
proofSteps: The diagram of the rows 0 → H¹_ur(K, A) → H¹(K, A) → H¹(I, A) for A = T, V, W gives H¹_f(W) ⊆ H¹_ur(W) and H¹_ur(T) ⊆ H¹_f(T) (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1's long exact sequences).

The image of V^I in W^I is (W^I)_div; taking I-cohomology and Frobenius invariants of 0 → T → V → W → 0 gives 0 → 𝒲^{Fr=1} → H¹(I, T)^{Fr=1} → H¹(I, V)^{Fr=1}, and with unramified-condition this gives (iii); (i), (ii) follow since 𝒲 is finite; (iv) since W^I = W is divisible when T is unramified.
Image of H¹_f(K, T): the diagram H¹(K, T) → H¹(K, W_M) → H²(K, T) over H¹(K, V) → H¹(K, W) → H²(K, T) (Rubin Lemma 3.8).
Archimedean: H¹(K, V) = 0 (Rubin Remark 3.7).
acceptance: These are the unramified and bad-prime comparison terms the L1 stage asks for; they are planned here because the conditions are L2's.

nodes.title: Local duality for the finite condition on V
nodes.statement: If K is archimedean, or nonarchimedean of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, then H¹_f(K, V) and H¹_f(K, V^*) are exact orthogonal complements under the local Tate pairing.
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p or K archimedean.
proofSteps: Archimedean K: all the groups vanish.
The pairing of two unramified classes factors through H²(K^ur/K, Φ(1)) = 0, as Gal(K^ur/K) has cohomological dimension 1.

dim H¹_f(K, V^*) = dim H⁰(K, V^*) = dim H²(K, V) = dim H¹(K, V) − dim H¹_f(K, V), by unramified-dimension-count, local duality for V (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4) and unramified-dimension-count again; conclude with orthogonal-complement's dimension count.
acceptance: The dimension count, not only orthogonality, is proved.

nodes.title: Local duality for the finite conditions on T and W_M
nodes.statement: Suppose K is archimedean, or nonarchimedean of residue characteristic ℓ ≠ p, or nonarchimedean with ℓ = p and H¹_f(K, V), H¹_f(K, V^*) chosen to be orthogonal complements. Then H¹_f(K, T) and H¹_f(K, W^*) are exact orthogonal complements, and so are H¹_f(K, W_M) and H¹_f(K, W^*_M) for every nonzero M ∈ O. In particular, for T unramified and ℓ ≠ p, the unramified conditions on T and T^* are exact annihilators (Mazur–Rubin, Proposition 1.7(i)).
hypotheses: The case ℓ = p needs the chosen orthogonal pair H¹_f(K, V), H¹_f(K, V^*).
proofSteps: lattice-pairing-compatibility: ⟨φ(c), d⟩ = ⟨c, φ^*(d)⟩.

By finite-condition-rational-duality (or the hypothesis at ℓ = p), H¹_f(K, V)^⊥ = H¹_f(K, V^*). Since H¹_f(K, W^*) = φ^*(H¹_f(K, V^*)) and H¹_f(K, T) = φ^{−1}(H¹_f(K, V)) (lattice-passage), orthogonal-complement's image/preimage rule gives H¹_f(K, W^*)^⊥ = H¹_f(K, T).
For W_M, use T ↠ W_M and W^*_M ↪ W^* in the same way, with H¹_f(K, W_M) the image of H¹_f(K, T) (finite-unramified-comparison).
Unramified T with ℓ ≠ p: finite-unramified-comparison (iv) identifies the finite and unramified conditions; at finite level this agrees with ArithmeticGaloisDuality's unramified-exact-annihilators.
acceptance: At ℓ = p nothing is claimed without the chosen orthogonal pair; that Bloch–Kato's subspaces for potentially semistable V are such a pair (Rubin, Remark 7.1) belongs to L4.

nodes.title: Selmer groups of T and W as limits
nodes.statement: For a finite set Σ of places: (i) S^Σ(K, T) = lim_M S^Σ(K, W_M) and S_Σ(K, T) = lim_M S_Σ(K, W_M); (ii) S^Σ(K, W) = colim_M S^Σ(K, W_M) and S_Σ(K, W) = colim_M S_Σ(K, W_M); the finite and singular parts of the local cohomology commute with these limits. The map ι_M : H¹(K, W_M) → H¹(K, W) induces a surjection S^Σ(K, W_M) ↠ S^Σ(K, W)[M], which can fail for S_Σ. S^Σ(K, W_M) is finite, S^Σ(K, T) is finitely generated over O, and the Pontryagin dual of S^Σ(K, W) is finitely generated over O.
hypotheses: Σ finite; T a lattice unramified outside a finite set.
proofSteps: H¹(K, W) = colim_M H¹(K, W_M), and H¹(K, T) = lim_M H¹(K, W_M) by Tate's inverse-limit theorem (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1/tate-inverse-limit; the H⁰ are finite).
The local groups at level M are finite, so the finite parts and singular quotients commute with the limits (Rubin, Corollary 3.10, using finite-unramified-comparison's description of H¹_f(K, W_M)).
ι_M(H¹(K, W_M)) = H¹(K, W)[M], and ι_M^{−1}(S^Σ(K, W)[M]) = S^Σ(K, W_M) by definition; for S_Σ the strict condition at Σ is not preserved under ι_M^{−1} (Rubin, Remark 5.5).
Enlarging Σ, S^Σ(K, A) = H¹(K_Σ/K, A) (galois-selmer-group), which is finite for A = W_M (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.3/h1-finite); the other two statements follow by the limits.
acceptance: Both the relaxed and the strict Selmer groups are covered, with the failure of Lemma 5.4 for the strict ones recorded.

nodes.title: Poitou–Tate for Selmer groups
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, T a p-adic representation of G_K ramified at finitely many primes, with H¹_f(K_v, V) and H¹_f(K_v, V^*) orthogonal complements at the places above p; let M ∈ O be nonzero and Σ_0 ⊆ Σ finite sets of places. (i) 0 → S^{Σ_0}(K, W_M) → S^Σ(K, W_M) → ⊕_{v∈Σ−Σ_0} H¹_s(K_v, W_M) and 0 → S_Σ(K, W^*_M) → S_{Σ_0}(K, W^*_M) → ⊕_{v∈Σ−Σ_0} H¹_f(K_v, W^*_M) are exact. (ii) The images loc^s(S^Σ(K, W_M)) and loc^f(S_{Σ_0}(K, W^*_M)) are exact orthogonal complements under Σ_{v∈Σ−Σ_0}⟨ , ⟩_v. (iii) S_{Σ_0}(K, W^*_M)/S_Σ(K, W^*_M) ≅ Hom_O(coker(loc^s_{Σ,Σ_0}), O/MO); in particular |S_{Σ_0}(K, W^*_M)| = |coker(loc^s_{Σ,Σ_0})| when S_Σ(K, W^*_M) = 0.
hypotheses: Orthogonal finite conditions at the places above p; Σ_0 ⊆ Σ finite.
proofSteps: (i) is immediate from the definitions (change-of-conditions).

For Σ containing the archimedean places, the places above p and the ramified primes, S^Σ(K, A) = H¹(K_Σ/K, A) (galois-selmer-group). The segment H¹(G_Σ, W_M) → P¹_Σ(K, W_M) → H¹(G_Σ, W^*_M)^∨ of Poitou–Tate (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4/poitou-tate), finite-condition-lattice-duality (H¹_s(W_M) is dual to H¹_f(W^*_M), by orthogonal-complement's quotient pairing) and the dual of the tautological sequence for S_Σ(K, W^*_M) splice to the exact sequence 0 → S^{Σ_0} → S^Σ → ⊕ H¹_s → S_{Σ_0}(W^*_M)^∨ → S_Σ(W^*_M)^∨ → 0, whose exactness in the centre is (ii).
General Σ: take Σ′ ⊇ Σ large; the snake lemma on the diagram for Σ_0 ⊆ Σ′ and Σ ⊆ Σ′ gives the sequence for Σ_0 ⊆ Σ (the map there is (loc^f_{Σ,Σ_0})^∨, SelmerIwasawaCohomology/E3).
(iii) restates (ii).
acceptance: Uses the global duality of ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4; summing local pairings alone does not prove (ii).
The real places enter through ArithmeticGaloisDuality's modified groups, which agree with ordinary cohomology in degree 1.

nodes.statement: With Σ_p the places above p: S(K, W^*)/S_{Σ_p}(K, W^*) ≅ Hom_O(coker(loc^s_{Σ_p}), D), where loc^s_{Σ_p} : S^{Σ_p}(K, T) → ∏_{v|p} H¹_s(K_v, T).

proofSteps: selmer-structure-poitou-tate (iii) with Σ = Σ_p and Σ_0 = ∅ at each level M; take the direct limit over M.
selmer-limits identifies lim_M S(K, W^*_M)/S_{Σ_p}(K, W^*_M) with S(K, W^*)/S_{Σ_p}(K, W^*), lim_M S^{Σ_p}(K, W_M) with S^{Σ_p}(K, T), and the singular quotients.

All groups at level M are finite: Hom_O(−, O/MO) turns the inverse limit of the cokernels into the direct limit of their duals (Pontryagin duality), and the inverse limit of the cokernels is the cokernel of the limit, as lim¹ of finite groups vanishes (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1).

nodes.title: Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete local noetherian ring with finite residue field of characteristic p, G a profinite group, H a closed normal subgroup, Γ = G/H, 𝒰 the open subgroups U ⊇ H, and M an ind-admissible R[G]-module; M_U = M ⊗_R R[G/U]. RΓ_Iw(G, H; M) is the complex lim_U C^•_cont(G, M_U) of R̄-modules, R̄ = R⟦Γ⟧, and H^i_Iw(G, H; M) its cohomology. There is a spectral sequence E₂^{ij} = lim^{(i)}_{U,cor} H^j_cont(U, M) ⇒ H^{i+j}_Iw(G, H; M); if M is of finite type over R and G satisfies (F) (finite cohomology of finite modules on open subgroups), then H^j_Iw(G, H; M) = lim_{U,cor} H^j_cont(U, M). If moreover 𝒰 has a cofinal chain and p^∞ divides the pro-finite order of Γ, then H⁰_Iw(G, H; M) = 0.
hypotheses: R complete local noetherian; M of finite type over R for the corestriction-limit description; condition (F), which G_{K,S} and local Galois groups satisfy (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4/global-finiteness).
proofSteps: The transition maps C^•_cont(G, M_V) → C^•_cont(G, M_U) are surjective, so the projective system is weakly flabby and the first hypercohomology spectral sequence for lim collapses (Jannsen); the second is the stated one, with corestriction transitions by Shapiro's lemma at finite level (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 7).
Under (F) the terms are finite-length R-modules, so the higher derived limits vanish (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1/mittag-leffler-lim-one).
H⁰: M^{U_n} stabilises to N, and the corestrictions N → N are multiplication by [U_n : U_{n′}], whose p-part tends to infinity; so the limit vanishes (Rubin, Lemma B.3.2).
acceptance: H⁰_Iw = 0 is a consequence of p^∞ | #Γ, not an assumption; torsion of H²_Iw is not asserted here (see iwasawa-torsion-criterion).

nodes.title: Shapiro's lemma for Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: With 𝓕_Γ(M) = lim_U M_U: for M of finite type over R there are canonical R̄[G]-isomorphisms 𝓕_Γ(M) ≅ (M ⊗_R R̄) ⟨−1⟩ and 𝓕_Γ(M)^ι ≅ (M ⊗_R R̄^ι)⟨−1⟩ ≅ (M ⊗_R R̄)⟨1⟩, where ⟨n⟩ twists the G-action by χ_Γ^n, χ_Γ : G → Γ ⊂ R̄^× the tautological character, and ι is the involution γ ↦ γ^{−1}; 𝓕_Γ(M) is of finite type over R̄. The canonical morphism C^•_cont(G, 𝓕_Γ(M)) → lim_U C^•_cont(G, M_U) is an isomorphism, so RΓ_cont(G, 𝓕_Γ(M)) ≅ RΓ_Iw(G, H; M).
hypotheses: M ind-admissible of finite type over R; Γ abelian, Γ ≅ Γ₀ × Δ with Γ₀ ≅ ℤ_p^r and Δ finite.
proofSteps: N ⊗_R R̄ = N ⊗_R lim R_U ≅ lim (N ⊗_R R_U) for N of finite type; on 𝓕_Γ(M), x ∈ R̄ acts by id ⊗ ι(x) and g ∈ G by g ⊗ χ_Γ(g), which gives the two isomorphisms (Nekovář 8.4.4.1).

The two projective-limit topologies on 𝓕_Γ(M), the m̄-adic and the (U, n)-adic, coincide, because {m̄^N} and {J_U + m^n R̄} are cofinal (J_U = ker(R̄ → R[G/U])); so continuous cochains commute with the limit (8.4.4.2).
acceptance: The inverse action is explicit: with the tautological character the Galois action on T ⊗ Λ is g ⊗ χ_Γ(g)^{−1}, as the stage and Burungale–Tian's items require; the opposite convention is 𝓕_Γ(M)^ι.

nodes.title: Descent and control for Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: (i) For M supported at the maximal ideal there is the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence E₂^{ij} = H^i_cont(Γ, H^j_cont(H, M)) ⇒ H^{i+j}_cont(G, M). (ii) If Γ ≅ ℤ_p^r, then RΓ_Iw(G, H; T) ⊗^L_{R̄} R ≅ RΓ_cont(G, T), with a homological spectral sequence E²_{ij} = H_{i,cont}(Γ, H^{−j}_Iw(G, H; T)) ⇒ H^{−i−j}_cont(G, T), each term of finite type over R when G satisfies (F). If Γ ≅ ℤ_p it degenerates into 0 → H^j_Iw(G, H; T)_Γ → H^j_cont(G, T) → H^{j+1}_Iw(G, H; T)^Γ → 0; and if cd_p(G) = e < ∞ and τ_{≤n}T ≅ T, then H^{e+n}_Iw(G, H; T)_Γ ≅ H^{e+n}_cont(G, T). (iii) For a closed Γ′ ≅ ℤ_p^{r′} in Γ with preimage H′, RΓ_Iw(G, H; T) ⊗^L R⟦Γ/Γ′⟧ ≅ RΓ_Iw(G, H′; T), with the analogous spectral sequence and, for Γ′ ≅ ℤ_p, the analogous short exact sequences.
hypotheses: Γ ≅ ℤ_p^r (or Γ′ ≅ ℤ_p^{r′}); T a bounded-below complex of finite type over R.
proofSteps: (i) is ArithmeticGaloisDuality's Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence (R02.2).

(ii) γ₁ − 1, …, γ_r − 1 is a regular sequence in R̄ with R̄/x ≅ R; tensoring the exact sequences 0 → R̄_{i−1} → R̄_{i−1} → R̄_i → 0 with T and applying iwasawa-shapiro gives the isomorphism; the Koszul filtration gives the spectral sequence (Nekovář 8.4.8.1).
For r = 1 the spectral sequence has two columns (8.4.8.2); (iii) replaces x by the generators of Γ′ (8.4.8.3–8.4.8.4).
acceptance: The control statements carry their error terms (coinvariants and invariants); no isomorphism H^j_Iw(G, H; T)_Γ ≅ H^j(G, T) is claimed in general.

nodes.title: A criterion for torsion Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: Assume Γ ≅ ℤ_p^r, G satisfies (F) and cd_p(G) < ∞. Let 𝔭 ∈ Spec(R) and 𝔭̄ ∈ Spec(R̄) its preimage under the augmentation R̄ → R. If T ∈ D^b of finite type over R has RΓ_cont(G, T)_𝔭 ≅ 0, then RΓ_cont(G, 𝓕_Γ(T))_𝔭̄ ≅ 0.
hypotheses: The vanishing of the specialised complex at 𝔭 is a hypothesis.
proofSteps: iwasawa-descent (ii) localised at 𝔭 gives E²_{ij} = H_{i,cont}(Γ, H^{−j})_𝔭 ⇒ H^{−i−j}_cont(G, T)_𝔭 = 0, with finitely many nonzero terms.
If E²_{0,j} = 0 then all E²_{i,j} = 0 (Nekovář 7.2.7 and Lemma 8.10.5); by induction on j, (H^{−j})_𝔭̄/J = 0 for the augmentation ideal J ⊆ 𝔭̄, and Nakayama's lemma gives H^{−j}_𝔭̄ = 0.
acceptance: This is the form in which torsion of H²_Iw and of Selmer duals is proved; it is a separate conclusion from a specialisation hypothesis, never a default (the stage's warning).

nodes.title: Universal norms are unramified away from p
nodes.statement: Let T be finitely generated over ℤ_p. (i) If K/ℚ_ℓ is finite with ℓ ≠ p and K_∞ its unramified ℤ_p-extension, every norm-compatible {c_F} ∈ lim H¹(F, T) has c_F ∈ H¹_ur(F, T). (ii) If K is a number field, K_∞/K abelian with Gal(K_∞/K) ≅ ℤ_p^d, and λ ∤ p a prime of F whose decomposition group in Gal(K_∞/K) is infinite, then (c_F)_λ ∈ H¹_ur(F_λ, T). (iii) If S contains the primes where T is ramified, those above p, those with finite decomposition group in Gal(K_∞/K) and the infinite places, then lim_F H¹(F, T) = lim_F H¹(K_S/F, T).
hypotheses: ℓ ≠ p in (i); d ≥ 1.
proofSteps: (i) 0 → H¹_ur(F, T) → H¹(F, T) → H¹(I, T)^{G_F}, with H¹(I, T) finitely generated over ℤ_p (Rubin, Proposition B.2.7(iii)); the limit of the last terms vanishes by iwasawa-cohomology's H⁰ statement (Lemma B.3.2).
(ii) Choose F′ ⊆ F_∞ with Gal(F_∞/F′) ≅ ℤ_p undecomposed at λ̄ and apply (i); corestrict.
(iii) By (ii) the restriction of c_F to each inertia group outside S vanishes, so its cocycles factor through Gal(K_S/F).
acceptance: Only for primes not above p; the places above p and those that split finitely are kept in S.

nodes.title: Semilocal cohomology and descent of local classes
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, q a prime of K, F/K finite and S the primes of F above q, with decomposition groups D_Q = g_Q^{−1} D g_Q. For a discrete G_K-module T and a D-submodule T′, H^i(F, Ind_D^{G_K}(T′)) ≅ ⊕_{Q∈S} H^i(F_Q, T′_Q); in particular H^i(G_F, Ind_D(T)) ≅ ⊕_Q H^i(F_Q, T) and H^i(G_F, Ind_D(T^I)) ≅ ⊕_Q H^i(F_Q, T^{I_Q}). For F/K finite Galois and T finitely generated over ℤ_p, restriction gives H¹(K_q, T) ≅ (⊕_{Q|q} H¹(F_Q, T))^{Gal(F/K)} if [F : K] is prime to p, and H¹(K_q, V) ≅ (⊕_{Q|q} H¹(F_Q, V))^{Gal(F/K)} always.
hypotheses: T discrete for the induction statements; finitely generated over ℤ_p for the descent.
proofSteps: D\G_K/G_F ↔ S by D g G_F ↦ g^{−1}Q₀; the double-coset form of Shapiro's lemma (Rubin, Proposition B.4.2; ProfiniteCohomology Layers 6–7) gives the decomposition.
Descent: ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2/finite-index-descent applied to the semilocal module; for V, finite groups have no rational cohomology.
acceptance: This is how infinite-level local conditions are defined: as limits of semilocal conditions, not as conditions over a 'completion' of K_∞.

nodes.title: Twisting Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: For the cyclotomic Γ = Gal(ℚ(ζ_{p^∞})/ℚ) with compatible roots (ζ_{p^n}) fixed, κ the cyclotomic character and k ∈ ℤ, cup product with the norm-compatible system (ζ_{p^n}^{⊗k})_n gives a ℤ_p-linear isomorphism φ_k : H^q_Iw(T) ≅ H^q_Iw(T(k)) with φ_k(λx) = Tw_k(λ)φ_k(x), where Tw_k is the ring automorphism of Λ = 𝒪⟦Γ⟧ with Tw_k(σ) = κ(σ)^{−k}σ. Composing with the specialisation of iwasawa-descent at the augmentation gives H¹_Iw(V) → H¹(ℤ[1/p], T(k)) ⊗ ℚ, which factors through the localisation at ker(Λ → 𝒪, σ_c ↦ c^{−k}).
hypotheses: Cyclotomic tower; compatible roots of unity fixed (they trivialise ℤ_p(1) over the tower).
proofSteps: The system (ζ_{p^n}^{⊗k}) is restriction-compatible, so by the projection formula cor(x ∪ res y) = cor(x) ∪ y the cup products are corestriction-compatible (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 12; ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2's cup products).
σ(x ∪ ζ^{⊗k}) = σx ∪ κ(σ)^kζ^{⊗k}, which is the Tw_k-semilinearity; the inverse is cup product with (ζ_{p^n}^{⊗−k}).
The specialisation is iwasawa-descent (ii); augmentation ∘ Tw_k sends σ_c to c^{−k}.
acceptance: Semilinear, not Λ-linear for an unchanged action (Burungale–Tian's warning); changing the compatible roots changes coordinates, not the module.

sources.match: The twist-and-specialise map (3.2), with the prime q of the proof of Theorem 3.1.

nodes.title: Local units and the cyclotomic Euler system in Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: For K_n = ℚ_p(μ_{p^n}), the local Kummer identifications K̂_n^× ≅ H^1(K_n, ℤ_p(1)) (p-adic completions; E1) intertwine norms with corestriction and give lim_n K̂_n^× ≅ lim_n H^1(K_n, ℤ_p(1)) = H^1_Iw(ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1)) (RJW (10.8), corrected). The inclusion of principal units gives κ : U_∞ → H^1_Iw(ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1)). The global classes z_m = δ(c_m) ∈ H^1(ℚ(μ_m), ℤ_p(1)) of the cyclotomic units c_m = (ξ_m^{−1} − 1)/(ξ_m − 1), m = Dp^n, satisfy cores(z_{mℓ}) = z_m for ℓ | m and (1 − Frob_ℓ^{−1})z_m for ℓ ∤ m, and their localisations at p along the tower m = Dp^n define a class in H^1_Iw(ℚ_p, ℤ_p(1)) (RJW §10.5, the cohomological reinterpretation of the Coleman map).
hypotheses: p odd; D ≥ 1 prime to p; completions as in SelmerIwasawaCohomology L0.
proofSteps: The finite-level Kummer isomorphisms K_n^×/(K_n^×)^{p^m} ≅ H^1(K_n, μ_{p^m}) commute with norm and corestriction; pass to the limit in m (L0/padic-kummer-identification, L0/local-completion) and then in n (L3/iwasawa-cohomology).
κ: U_∞ = lim U_n^1 maps to lim K̂_n^×; it is injective because each U_n^1 is ℤ_p-complete.

The corestriction relations are the Kummer images of the norm relations N(c_{mℓ}) = c_m (ℓ | m) and N(c_{mℓ}) = c_m^{1 − Frob_ℓ^{−1}} (ℓ ∤ m), which EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture L0 plans; RJW print the second as (1 − ℓ^{−1})c_m (finding E4).
Localisation at the place above p commutes with corestriction, so the classes loc_p(z_{Dp^n}) form an element of the limit.
acceptance: Coleman's map Col′ and Perrin-Riou's big logarithm, which RJW mention after (10.8), are owned by ColemanPowerSeries and PadicHodgeRegulators; they are not planned here.

nodes.title: Greenberg Selmer groups of Tate twists
nodes.statement: Give V_n = ℚ_p(n) the filtration Fil^iℚ_p(n) = ℚ_p(n) for i ≤ n and 0 for i > n. Then L^Gr_{v_p} = H^1(K_∞^+, W_n) for n ≥ 1 and L^Gr_{v_p} = H^1_ur(K_∞^+, W_n) for n ≤ 0. Inflation–restriction gives H^1(F, W_n) = Hom_{cts,{±1}}(G_{F_∞}, W_n), and hence H^1_{L^Gr}(F, W_n) = Hom_cts(X_∞^{c=(−1)^n}, W_n) for n ≥ 1 and Hom_cts(Y_∞^{c=(−1)^n}, W_n) for n ≤ 0. Since (X_∞)^{c=1} ≅ X_∞^+, for even n > 0, H^1_{L^Gr}(F, W_n) = Hom_cts(X_∞^+, W_n), whose Pontryagin dual is X_∞^+(−n), the module X_∞^+ with its Λ(Γ^+)-action twisted by χ^{−n} (RJW §13.5.2, Example 13.22).
hypotheses: p odd; F_∞ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞}), F = F_∞^+ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+, Gal(F_∞/F) = {1, c}; K_∞^+ = ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})^+ is the completion at the unique place v_p above p; χ is the cyclotomic character, T_n = ℤ_p(n), V_n = ℚ_p(n), W_n = (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)(n); X_∞ = Gal(M_∞/F_∞) and Y_∞ = Gal(L_∞/F_∞) for the maximal abelian pro-p extensions unramified outside p and everywhere unramified, with X_∞^+ = Gal(M_∞^+/F_∞^+) (IntegralIwasawaTheory L1).
proofSteps: Local condition: W_n/Fil^1W_n is 0 for n ≥ 1 and W_n for n ≤ 0, so L^Gr is everything or the unramified condition (L2/greenberg-condition).
G_{F_∞} acts trivially on W_n, so H^1(F_∞, W_n) = Hom_cts(G_{F_∞}, W_n); since #{1, c} = 2 is prime to p, inflation–restriction gives H^1(F, W_n) = Hom_cts(G_{F_∞}, W_n)^{{1,c}}.

A class is p-power torsion with abelian image, so it factors through the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F_∞; the unramified conditions away from p factor it through X_∞, and for n ≤ 0 the condition at p factors it through Y_∞.
c acts on W_n by (−1)^n and X_∞ = X_∞^{c=1} ⊕ X_∞^{c=−1} (p odd), so {±1}-equivariant homomorphisms are those on the (−1)^n-eigenspace; restriction identifies X_∞^{c=1} with X_∞^+.
Pontryagin duality with the contragredient action (L2/pontryagin-dual) turns Hom_cts(X_∞^+, W_n) into X_∞^+(−n).
acceptance: RJW write H^1_{L^Gr}(F_∞, W_n) for the group over F = F_∞^+ in steps (3)–(4), and "n ≥ 0" for n ≤ 0 (finding E5).
The odd-n and n ≤ 0 cases give the minus part of X_∞ and the parts of Y_∞; only even n > 0 recovers X_∞^+.

nodes.title: The Gamma factor, r_V and criticality
nodes.statement: For a p-adic representation V attached to an arithmetic object, with archimedean Euler factor L_∞(V, s) (a product of shifted Gamma functions without zeros), r_V is the order of the pole of L_∞(V, s) at s = 1, and V^∨ = Hom_cts(V, ℚ_p(1)) is the Tate dual. Greenberg's criticality hypothesis is r_V = r_{V^∨} = 0. For V = ℚ_p(n): L(V, s) = ζ(s − n) and L_∞(V, s) = π^{−(s−n)/2}Γ((s − n)/2), with poles at s = n, n − 2, …; so r_{ℚ_p(n)} = 1 if n is odd and positive and 0 otherwise, V^∨ = ℚ_p(1 − n), and ℚ_p(n) is critical exactly when n is even and positive or odd and negative (RJW Remark 13.23).
hypotheses: V is given together with its Gamma factor; the general recipe from Hodge data is listed as remaining.
proofSteps: r_{ℚ_p(n)}: s = 1 is a pole of Γ((s − n)/2) iff (1 − n)/2 ∈ {0, −1, −2, …} iff n is odd and n ≥ 1.
r_{ℚ_p(n)^∨} = r_{ℚ_p(1−n)} = 1 iff 1 − n is odd and positive iff n is even and n ≤ 0.
Both vanish iff (n even or n ≤ 0) and (n odd or n ≥ 1), i.e. n even with n ≥ 2, or n odd with n ≤ −1.
acceptance: This is Greenberg's Gamma-factor notion; it agrees with Deligne's criticality for Tate twists (L(ℚ_p(n), 1) = ζ(1 − n) and L(ℚ_p(n)^∨, 1) = ζ(n) both critical).

nodes.title: The Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture (as a proposition)
nodes.statement: Let V be a p-ordinary representation of G_ℚ (a saturated G_ℚ-stable filtration Fil^iV with I_{ℚ_p} acting on Fil^i/Fil^{i+1} by χ^i), T ⊆ V a G_ℚ-stable lattice and W = V/T, and suppose given a p-adic L-function L_p(V) in the fraction field of Λ(Γ^+) (conjectured by Coates–Perrin-Riou). The Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture for V is the conjunction of (i) the Λ(Γ^+)-corank of H^1_{L^Gr}(F, W) equals r_V, and (ii) if r_V = r_{V^∨} = 0, the characteristic ideal of the Pontryagin dual of H^1_{L^Gr}(F, W) is (L_p(V)) (RJW Conjecture 13.21, after Greenberg). These are propositions; no node assumes them, and the existence of L_p(V) is part of the data, not a theorem.
hypotheses: V p-ordinary at p (Greenberg filtration, stable under G_{ℚ_p}; see E2); L_p(V) is supplied data.
proofSteps: Definitions only: (i) uses the corank (L2/corank) and (ii) the characteristic ideal of a finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ^+)-module (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4, with the isotypic decomposition over Λ(Γ^+)).
acceptance: The rank-zero characteristic-ideal statement (ii) and any positive-rank leading-term statement are distinct propositions; only (i) and (ii) are stated.
RJW state the conjecture over F = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+, not over the cyclotomic ℤ_p-extension used by Greenberg (their Remark 13.9).

nodes.title: Greenberg's conjecture for even Tate twists is the Iwasawa main conjecture
nodes.statement: For V = ℚ_p(n) with n even and positive, V is critical and the Pontryagin dual of H^1_{L^Gr}(F, W_n) is X_∞^+(−n); Greenberg's p-adic L-function is the nth twist of the Kubota–Leopoldt p-adic zeta function; and Conjecture 13.21(ii) for V is equivalent to the Iwasawa main conjecture (RJW Theorem 13.8), hence holds (Example 13.22). Conjecture 13.21(i) holds as well, since X_∞^+ is Λ(Γ^+)-torsion. The case n = 0 is not covered: r_{ℚ_p(1)} = 1 (Remark 13.23).
hypotheses: p odd; F_∞ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞}), F = F_∞^+ = ℚ(μ_{p^∞})^+, Gal(F_∞/F) = {1, c}; K_∞^+ = ℚ_p(μ_{p^∞})^+ is the completion at the unique place v_p above p; χ is the cyclotomic character, T_n = ℤ_p(n), V_n = ℚ_p(n), W_n = (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)(n); X_∞ = Gal(M_∞/F_∞) and Y_∞ = Gal(L_∞/F_∞) for the maximal abelian pro-p extensions unramified outside p and everywhere unramified, with X_∞^+ = Gal(M_∞^+/F_∞^+) (IntegralIwasawaTheory L1).
proofSteps: criticality gives r_V = r_{V^∨} = 0 for even n > 0; tate-twist-greenberg-selmer gives the dual X_∞^+(−n).

Twisting by χ^{−n} is a ring automorphism of Λ(Γ^+), and characteristic ideals transform by it (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L4, characteristic-ideal); so char(X_∞^+(−n)) is the nth twist of char(X_∞^+).
Theorem 13.8 (EulerSystemsCyclotomicMainConjecture L3) identifies char(X_∞^+) with the ideal of the Kubota–Leopoldt ζ_p; twisting gives (ii).
(i): X_∞^+ is a finitely generated torsion Λ(Γ^+)-module (Iwasawa), so the corank is 0 = r_V.
acceptance: This is the acceptance item "RJW §13.5" of the stage: the even-positive restriction is proved from the parity table, and n = 0 is excluded as the source says.

nodes.title: The Bloch–Kato local condition on T and W
nodes.statement: For a finite place v above p and V a de Rham representation of G_{F_v}, H^1_f(F_v, V) = ker(H^1(F_v, V) → H^1(F_v, V ⊗ B_cris)) (supplied by PadicHodgeRegulators L1), and the Bloch–Kato condition on W = V/T is L^BK_v = im(H^1_f(F_v, V) → H^1(F_v, W)), with its preimage on T (RJW Definition 13.19(2)). At places not above p the condition is unramified. Greenberg and Bloch–Kato conditions coincide in some fundamental examples, but not in general (Remark 13.20).
hypotheses: V a continuous representation of G_{F_v} on a finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector space with a stable lattice T.
proofSteps: Propagate the subspace H^1_f(F_v, V) ⊆ H^1(F_v, V) to T and W with L2/condition-propagation: the image in H^1(F_v, W) and the preimage in H^1(F_v, T).
Unramified at v ∤ p by definition; the global Selmer group is L2/galois-selmer-group for this Selmer structure.
acceptance: The comparison with Greenberg's condition (Kato; Perrin-Riou §2.4.7) is not read and is listed as remaining; no universal equality is asserted.

sourceIssues.printed: The source treats inverse limits over m ≥ 1 as exact and obtains the Kummer isomorphism δ : F× ⊗ Zp ∼−→ H1(F, Zp(1)). (10.7) It then applies the same procedure with Qp replacing Q and with F replaced by a finite extension Kn of Qp, for n ≥ 1, to obtain K×n ⊗ Zp ≅ H1(Kn, Zp(1)).
sourceIssues.correction: δ : lim_m F^×/(F^×)^{p^m} ≅ H^1(F, ℤ_p(1)), with the p-adic completion (Rubin's F^× ⊗̂ ℤ_p) in place of F^× ⊗ ℤ_p; likewise for K_n. The limit step holds because lim^1_m μ_{p^m}(F) = 0 (finite groups; Rubin Proposition B.2.3), not because inverse limits are exact.
sourceIssues.reason: For a number field F, F^× contains a free abelian group on infinitely many primes, and a p-adic Cauchy sequence such as ∏_{i≤m} ℓ_i^{p^i} involves infinitely many primes, so it is not in the image of F^× ⊗ ℤ_p: the map is not surjective. For K/ℚ_p finite, U^1_K ⊇ ℤ_p and ℤ_p ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p → ℤ_p kills a ⊗ 1 − 1 ⊗ a, which is nonzero for a ∈ ℤ_p ∖ ℚ since ℤ_p ⊗_ℤ ℤ_p embeds in ℚ_p ⊗_ℚ ℚ_p: the map is not injective. Inverse limits of abelian groups are not exact in general; the lim^1 term must be shown to vanish.
